You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 0f28ede906a8ad44158a6ef9471a5a412343cced Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: John Garry <john.garry@huawei.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jan 2016 01:31:17 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] hisi_sas: fix v1 hw check for slot error

Completion header bit CMPLT_HDR_RSPNS_XFRD flags whether the response
frame is received into host memory, and not whether the response frame
has an error.  As such, change the decision on whether a slot has an
error.  Also redundant check on CMPLT_HDR_CMD_CMPLT_MSK is removed.

Fixes: 27a3f229 ("hisi_sas: Add cq interrupt handler")

Signed-off-by: John Garry <john.garry@huawei.com>
Tested-by: Ricardo Salveti <ricardo.salveti@linaro.org>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>
---
 drivers/scsi/hisi_sas/hisi_sas_v1_hw.c | 9 +++------
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/scsi/hisi_sas/hisi_sas_v1_hw.c b/drivers/scsi/hisi_sas/hisi_sas_v1_hw.c
index d54381149c0d..d04808ef6b2b 100644
--- a/drivers/scsi/hisi_sas/hisi_sas_v1_hw.c
+++ b/drivers/scsi/hisi_sas/hisi_sas_v1_hw.c
@@ -1293,13 +1293,10 @@ static int slot_complete_v1_hw(struct hisi_hba *hisi_hba,
 		goto out;
 	}
 
-	if (cmplt_hdr_data & CMPLT_HDR_ERR_RCRD_XFRD_MSK) {
-		if (!(cmplt_hdr_data & CMPLT_HDR_CMD_CMPLT_MSK) ||
-		    !(cmplt_hdr_data & CMPLT_HDR_RSPNS_XFRD_MSK))
-			ts->stat = SAS_DATA_OVERRUN;
-		else
-			slot_err_v1_hw(hisi_hba, task, slot);
+	if (cmplt_hdr_data & CMPLT_HDR_ERR_RCRD_XFRD_MSK &&
+		!(cmplt_hdr_data & CMPLT_HDR_RSPNS_XFRD_MSK)) {
 
+		slot_err_v1_hw(hisi_hba, task, slot);
 		goto out;
 	}
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect interpretation of the completion header bits in the hardware response. Specifically, the code was mistakenly using the `CMPLT_HDR_RSPNS_XFRD` bit to determine if a slot had an error, rather than checking for the actual error condition indicated by the `CMPLT_HDR_ERR_RCRD_XFRD` bit. This led to erroneous handling of slot errors, as the presence of a response frame in host memory was incorrectly equated with the absence of an error. The patch corrects this logic by ensuring that a slot is only marked as having an error if the error record bit is set and the response frame has not been received.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect interpretation of the completion header bits in the hardware response. Specifically, the code was mistakenly using the `CMPLT_HDR_RSPNS_XFRD` bit to determine if a slot had an error, rather than checking for the actual error condition indicated by the `CMPLT_HDR_ERR_RCRD_XFRD` bit. This led to erroneous handling of slot errors, as the presence of a response frame in host memory was incorrectly equated with the absence of an error. The patch corrects this logic by ensuring that a slot is only marked as having an error if the error record bit is set and the response frame has not been received.
